metaTitle: Business Travel in Dubai: A Day of Meetings by Chauffeur
metaDescription: Planning a day of meetings in Dubai? How to order them around traffic, when to book a chauffeur by the hour, which car to choose and what to have ready.
excerpt: A day of back-to-back meetings in Dubai is easy with one chauffeur and a bit of planning. This guide covers how to order your meetings around traffic, whether to book by the hour or as transfers, and which car suits a business day.
quickAnswer: Book one chauffeur by the hour, group your meetings by district and keep the long crossings out of the morning and evening rush. The car waits outside each address, tolls and parking are handled, and you can add stops as the day changes. Emirates Limo's hourly service starts from AED 150 per hour, with the same driver and car for the whole day.
content:
The simplest way to run a day of meetings in Dubai is to book one chauffeur by the hour and let the car wait outside each address, rather than chasing a separate taxi after every meeting. Group your meetings by district, keep the long crossings out of the morning and evening peaks, and you will get through five or six appointments without once thinking about parking. Emirates Limo runs this as an hourly service from AED 150 per hour, with the same driver and car for the whole day.

What should I have ready before I book a chauffeur for a day of meetings?

A chauffeur day works best when the driver knows the plan before the first pickup. Five minutes with your calendar the night before saves an hour of phone calls the next day.

  • Every meeting address in full: building name, tower and area, not just a company name or a map pin
  • Start and end times for each meeting, plus a realistic buffer for the ones that always overrun
  • Your hotel or home address for the first pickup and the final drop-off
  • The number of people travelling with you and whether anyone joins or leaves mid-day
  • Any luggage or sample cases you are carrying, which decides whether a sedan is enough
  • A working UAE-reachable phone number, so the chauffeur can message you when the car is at the door
  • Your flight number if the day starts at DXB or DWC, so the pickup follows the flight

How do I plan the order of meetings around Dubai traffic?

Group by district first, then fix the order. Dubai's business addresses cluster into a few zones: DIFC and Downtown, Business Bay, Sheikh Zayed Road towers, Media City and Internet City, JLT and Marina, and the free zones out towards Jebel Ali and Dubai South. Moving within one zone takes minutes; crossing from Deira to Jebel Ali in the wrong hour can take well over an hour.

The road that matters is Sheikh Zayed Road (E11), the coastal spine that links almost every business district, with Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Road (E311) as the inland alternative. The UAE Government portal describes E11 as the country's longest road and E311 as the inland route through Dubai and the Northern Emirates. Your chauffeur will pick between them on the day depending on what the traffic apps show.

Book the meetings furthest from your hotel for the middle of the day, when the roads are at their quietest. Early morning and late afternoon are the rush hours, so an 8am start in DIFC when you are staying in Marina means leaving with time to spare. A late afternoon meeting near Jebel Ali followed by dinner in Downtown is the classic mistake, because you will be driving into the city with everyone else.

Should I book a chauffeur by the hour or as separate transfers?

For three or more stops in a day, book by the hour. An hourly chauffeur in Dubai from Emirates Limo starts from AED 150 per hour, the driver and car stay with you for the whole booking, and you can add as many stops as you like without re-booking. If a meeting finishes early, you leave early; if it runs long, the car is still outside.

Separate point-to-point transfers make sense when your day is really two fixed moves: hotel to office in the morning, office to airport in the evening. Each of those comes with 15 minutes of free waiting at the pickup, which is fine for a lobby collection but not for a meeting that might overrun. A private transfer within Dubai is priced as a fixed fare at booking, so there is no meter running while you wait for the lift.

The middle option is a half-day hourly booking for the meetings, then a single transfer to the airport at the end. Plenty of business travellers do exactly that, and the chauffeur service page covers both formats.

Which car should I book for a business day?

For one or two people with laptop bags, any of the sedans works and the choice is about the back seat. For a team of four or more, or if you are carrying sample cases, go straight to the SUV or a van so nobody is balancing a bag on their knees between meetings.

What happens with tolls, parking and waiting time during the day?

Nothing that involves you. Dubai's main roads carry Salik toll gates and, according to the UAE Government portal, the toll varies with the time of day you pass through. Every Emirates Limo fare already includes Salik and Darb tolls, VAT and any other taxes, so nothing is collected in the car and the price you saw at booking is the price you pay.

Parking is the chauffeur's problem, not yours. You are dropped at the tower entrance, the driver finds somewhere to wait, and the car is back at the door when you message. In DIFC, Downtown and Business Bay that alone can save twenty minutes per meeting compared with driving yourself.

On an hourly booking, waiting is simply part of the time you have paid for. On a point-to-point transfer the free waiting is 15 minutes, or 60 minutes at the airport counted from the actual landing time. If your day involves long, unpredictable meetings, that difference is the reason to book by the hour.

Can I fit Abu Dhabi meetings into the same day?

Yes, if you treat it as a half day. Abu Dhabi is around 90 minutes from central Dubai each way on a clear road, so a morning of Dubai meetings followed by two appointments in Abu Dhabi and a drive back is a long but perfectly normal day with a chauffeur. The car becomes the office for the drive, which is when most people catch up on calls.

Abu Dhabi has its own toll system, Darb, on the four bridges into the city. The UAE Government portal lists the peak windows as 7am to 9am and 3pm to 7pm; the Abu Dhabi Mobility Darb page confirms the AED 4 charge applies in those windows except on Sundays and official holidays. That is included in your fare too, but it tells you when the bridges are busiest, so aim to cross outside those windows.

If the Abu Dhabi leg is the whole afternoon, a dedicated Dubai to Abu Dhabi transfer is the cleaner booking, with the return as a second transfer or an hourly block in the capital through the Abu Dhabi chauffeur service.

How do public holidays and the working week affect a Dubai business trip?

Check the holiday calendar before you book flights, not after. The UAE Government portal lists National Day on 2 and 3 December, Eid Al Fitr, Eid Al Adha and the other Islamic holidays, and notes that the Islamic dates follow the moon sighting, so they are only confirmed close to the day. Offices empty out, and the roads out of Dubai fill up the evening before.

Friday is the quiet end of the working week in the UAE, with many offices on shorter hours, so if you can only get one day of meetings, Tuesday or Wednesday will give you the fullest diaries. Emirates Limo runs 24 hours a day, every day, including public holidays, so the chauffeur side of the plan does not change even when the calendar does.

What goes wrong on a day of meetings in Dubai?

Booking meetings in geographical order rather than traffic order. A neat line from Deira to Jebel Ali reads well on a map, but it puts the longest drive at the busiest time. Put the far-away meeting in the middle of the day.

Sending the driver a company name instead of an address. Business Bay alone has dozens of towers with similar names. Send the building, the tower and the area, and add the client's phone number in case the entrance is on a different street.

Booking point-to-point transfers for a day that keeps changing. Each transfer has a fixed pickup time and 15 minutes of free waiting. When the 11am slips to 11:40, the hourly booking absorbs it and the transfer does not.

Forgetting the airport leg. If you are flying out that evening, put the flight time in the plan and work backwards. The chauffeur will tell you when to leave the last meeting, and if the day starts at the airport, a Dubai airport transfer with flight tracking gets you into the city without the taxi queue.

Cancelling late. Cancel 24 hours or more before the pickup time and you get a full refund; inside 24 hours, and for no-shows, the booking is charged in full. If a trip is in doubt, make the call the day before.

Relying on the metro for a tight schedule. The Dubai Metro is excellent, and Dubai Airports notes the Red Line runs straight from Terminals 1 and 3, but it does not stop outside most office towers and you will still need a taxi at each end. It is a fine backup, not a plan.

faqs.question: Is it better to book a chauffeur by the hour or per trip for meetings in Dubai?
faqs.answer: By the hour, if you have three or more stops. The driver and car stay with you, stops are unlimited and a meeting that overruns costs you nothing extra in hassle. Point-to-point transfers suit a day with just two fixed moves.

faqs.question: How much does an hourly chauffeur in Dubai cost?
faqs.answer: Emirates Limo's hourly chauffeur service starts from AED 150 per hour. The exact price depends on the car you choose and the number of hours, and it is fixed at booking with tolls and VAT included.

faqs.question: Does the chauffeur wait while I am in a meeting?
faqs.answer: Yes. On an hourly booking the car waits for as long as you need, because the time is already yours. On a single transfer you get 15 minutes of free waiting at the pickup, or 60 minutes at an airport.

faqs.question: Are Salik tolls charged separately on a chauffeur booking?
faqs.answer: No. Every Emirates Limo fare includes Salik and Darb tolls, VAT and any other taxes. The price you see at booking is the full price and nothing is collected in the car.

faqs.question: Can I add an Abu Dhabi meeting to a Dubai chauffeur day?
faqs.answer: Yes. Abu Dhabi is around 90 minutes from central Dubai each way, so it works as a half-day leg. Book it as part of the hourly service or as a dedicated Dubai to Abu Dhabi transfer, and try to cross the Abu Dhabi bridges outside the Darb peak hours.
